item.title: How the Pentagon Is Getting Into the Venezuelan Oil Business Under Trump
item.description: The Defense Department’s Office of Strategic Capital, founded by the Biden administration to give loans to bolster the U.S. defense industry, is helping lead President Trump’s oil deal.

item.title: Whistle-Blower Says Trump Officials Are Defying Court Orders on Voting by Mail
item.description: A report detailed “grave concerns” that a new system being rushed into use by the U.S. Postal Service could imperil millions of mail ballots ahead of the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron

item.title: C.D.C. Director Challenges Pennsylvania’s Report of Two Measles Deaths
item.description: Questioning a state’s investigation is highly unusual for the public health agency, but reflects tensions between the Trump administration and many states over health issues.
item.dc:creator: Apoorva Mandavilli and Teddy Rosenbluth
item.category: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
item.media:description: Dr. Erica Schwartz, who has expressed strong support of childhood vaccines, was confirmed as C.D.C. director this month, despite persistent questions during her confirmation hearing about her willingness and ability to push back against Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s actions.

item.title: How the Supreme Court Locks Away Its Own History
item.description: After Justice Scalia died, the justices held private negotiations about locking away their papers. We may not see the ultimate record of the Roberts court for decades.

item.title: Supreme Court Allows Trump’s White House Ballroom Construction
item.description: Lower-court rulings would have blocked construction of the 90,000-square-foot ballroom after finding that the Trump administration should have first sought approval from Congress.
item.dc:creator: Ann E. Marimow
item.category: White House East Wing and Ballroom (Washington, DC)
item.media:description: The order from the Supreme Court was the second time in less than two weeks that the court weighed in on the project.

item.title: Duane Davis Is Convicted of Orchestrating Tupac Shakur’s Murder
item.description: Duane Keith Davis, 63, was found guilty of first-degree murder after he went on an interview tour discussing his role in the 1996 drive-by shooting.
item.dc:creator: Julia Jacobs and Anusha Bayya
item.media:description: Duane Keith Davis, right, and his lawyer, Michael Sanft, after a jury found Mr. Davis guilty. He faces up to life in prison.

item.title: Who Is Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis, Convicted in Tupac Shakur Murder Trial?
item.description: Duane Keith Davis, once a high-ranking member of the South Side Compton Crips, long said he was in a Cadillac with the shooter in 1996. Then he began to recant his accounts.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Abrams
item.media:description: Duane Keith Davis was convicted of murder in the 1996 shooting death of Tupac Shakur.

item.title: Tupac Shakur Was at His Cultural Peak When He Was Killed

item.title: China Censors and Punishes to Shape Narrative on Floods in Tibet, a Contrast to Nepal

item.title: A Principal Saved 900 Students Before His School Was Washed Away in Nepal
item.description: Rajendra Dawadi had less than 15 minutes to act on a warning of approaching floodwaters. His swift evacuation plan saved hundreds of lives.
item.dc:creator: Binod Ghimire and Claire Moses
item.media:description: Rajendra Dawadi was teaching at the Tribhuvan Trishuli School when a staff member burst into the classroom, shouting that a major flood was headed their way.
